extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / mathematicians / physicists (readers of Newton's Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the individual propositions, corollaries, and methodological statements in Newton's Principia (Latin) about attraction by cylinders/spheroids, analogies to optics (refraction/reflection), and motion in media with resistance (linear and quadratic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder attraction (Corol. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unde si solidum Cylindrus sit, parallelogrammo ADEB circa axem AB revoluto descriptus, & vires centripetæ in singula ejus puncta tendentes sint reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum a punctis: erit attractio corpusculi P in hunc Cylindrum ut BA - PE + PD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: by integrating ordinatim applied FK one gets two area contributions along AB and PB/PA whose difference yields area LABI equal to 1 in AB - PE + PD, hence the attracting force is proportional to AB - PE + PD. The text includes the geometric area argument and references Prop. XC for the construction of FK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spheroid external-axis attraction formula (Corol. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc etiam vis innotescit qua Sphærois AGBCD attrahit corpus quodvis P, exterius in axe suo AB situm. ... vis qua Sphærois trahit corpus P erit ad vim qua Sphæra, diametro AB descripta, trahit idem corpus, ut AS × CSq. - PS × KMRK / (PSq. + CSq. - ASq.) ad AS cub. / 3PS quad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the ratio (formulaic relation) between the attraction of a spheroid and that of a sphere of diameter AB on an external point P on the axis. The statement is algebraic/geometric and indicates the method by computing segment areas (KMRK etc.) and using centres/semidiameter SC; notes that by the same computation one can find the forces of spheroid segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spheroid internal linear attraction (Corol. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod si corpusculum intra Sphæroidem in data quavis ejusdem diametro collocetur; attractio erit ut ipsius distantia a centro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: by decomposing concentric similar spheroids and cancelling opposite contributions, only the innermost spheroid matters, so attraction inside a spheroid is proportional to distance from center (linear restoring force). References Prop. LXXII and uses geometric partitioning into cones/segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing a body with prescribed pointwise centripetal decrement (Prop. XCII, Prob. XLVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dato corpore attractivo, invenire rationem decrementi virium centripetarum in ejus puncta singula tendentium. E corpore dato formanda est Sphæra vel Cylindrus aliave figura regularis, cujus lex attractionis, cuivis decrementi rationi congruens (per Prop. LXXX. LXXXI. & XCI.) inveniri potest. Dein factis experimentis invenienda est vis attractionis in diversis distantiis, & lex attractionis in totum inde patefacta dabit rationem decrementi virium partium singularum, quam invenire oportuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological prescription: choose a regular figure whose pointwise attraction law matches the desired decrement; then by experimental determination of attraction at various distances deduce the local decrement law. References earlier propositions for construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attraction of half-infinite solids and power-law decrease (Prop. XCIII, Theor. XLVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si solidum ex una parte planum, ex reliquis autem partibus infinitum, constet ex particulis æqualibus æqualiter attractivis, quarum vires in recessu a solido decrescunt in ratione potestatis cujusvis distantiarum plusquam quadraticæ, & vi solidi totius corpusculum ad utramvis plani partem constitutum trahatur: dico quod solidi vis illa attractiva, in recessu ab ejus superficie plana, decrescet in ratione potestatis, cujus latus est distantia corpusculi a plano, & Index ternario minor quam Index potestatis distantiarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed cases: Case 1 derives that if pointwise forces ∝ r^{-n} with n>3, total attraction from the solid behaves ∝ distance^{-(n-3)} (area/quadrature argument). Case 2 treats a particle inside the solid near the plane and finds attraction ∝ CK^{n-3}. Corollaries extend to infinite slabs and discuss when contributions of remote parts can be neglected. Scholium notes exception for n=3 (triplicate power) where assertion fails because remote part's attraction dominates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series expansion method for motion under power-law ordinates (Scholium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationes autem contrahi solent resolvendo ordinatim applicatas in series convergentes. ... resolvo in Seriem infinitam A^{m÷n} + m ÷ n OA^{(m-n)÷n} + {mm - mn} ÷ 2nn O^2 A^{(m - 2n)÷n} &c. ... Ut si ordinatim applicata Parabolam attingat, existente m = 2, & n = 1: fiet vis ut data 2B^0 ... Quod si ordinatim applicata Hyperbolam attingat, existente m = 0 - 1, & n = 1; fiet vis ut 2B^3: adeoq; vi, quæ sit ut cubus ordinatim applicatæ, corpus movebitur in Hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes using binomial/series expansion of (A+O)^{m/n} to resolve applied ordinates into power series; links particular exponent choices to known trajectories (parabola, hyperbola) and recovers Galileo's result for parabolic motion and an analogous result for hyperbolic applied ordinate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sine-law relation for incidence and emergence between two similar media (Prop. XCIV, Theor. XLVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si media duo similaria, spatio planis parallelis utrinq; terminato, distinguantur ab invicem, & corpus in transitu per hoc spatium attrahatur vel impellatur perpendiculariter versus medium alterutrum, neq; ulla alia vi agitetur vel impediatur; Sit autem attractio, in æqualibus ab utroq; plano distantiis ad eandem ipsius partem captis, ubiq; eadem: dico quod sinus incidentiæ in planum alterutrum erit ad sinum emergentiæ ex plano altero in ratione data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1 proves the proportion by geometric construction using parabolic motion in a uniform impulse; Case 2 extends to many planes and continuous limit yielding a continuous law. This is Newton's mechanical analogue to Snell's law: the ratio of sines of incidence/emergence is fixed by the media's action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity ratio equals sine ratio (Prop. XCV, Theor. XLIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis; dico quod velocitas corporis ante incidentiam est ad ejus velocitatem post emergentiam, ut sinus emergentiæ ad sinum incidentiæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates by decomposing motion into perpendicular and parallel components (Legum Corol. 2) that the speeds before and after passage relate as the sines of emergence and incidence respectively; relies on equal time intervals giving equal parallel displacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection when emergent velocity less than incident; equality of angles (Prop. XCVI, Theor. L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis & quod motus ante incidentiam velocior sit quam postea: dico quod corpus, inclinando lineam incidentiæ, reflectetur tandem, & angulus reflexionis fiet æqualis angulo incidentiæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that if the emergent path becomes tangent to a limiting plane (due to ratio of sines becoming unity relative to radius), the body cannot pass beyond and will be reflected; angle of reflection equals angle of incidence. Passage to continuous limit of many parallel planes secures the equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy between mechanical attraction-curved trajectories and optical refraction/reflection (Scholium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harum attractionum haud multum dissimiles sunt Lucis reflexiones & refractiones, factæ secundum datam Secantium rationem, ut invenit Snellius, & per consequens secundum datam Sinuum rationem, ut exposuit Cartesius. ... Radii autem in aere existentes ... in transitu suo prope corporum vel opacorum vel perspicuorum angulos ... incurvantur circum corpora, quasi attracti ... Fit igitur refractio, non in puncto incidentiæ, sed paulatim per continuam incurvationem radiorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newton notes the empirical observation of rays curving near bodies and interprets refraction as gradual curvature due to attraction (or medium action), suggesting mechanical models for optics; recommends applying subsequent propositions to optical uses while leaving nature of rays unsettled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of a refracting surface that focuses particles from A to B (Prop. XCVII, Prob. XLVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posito quod sinus incidentiæ in superficiem aliquam sit ad sinum emergentiæ in data ratione, quodq; incurvatio viæ corporum juxta superficiem illam fiat in spatio brevissimo ... determinare superficiem quæ corpuscula omnia de loco dato successive manantia convergere faciat ad alium locum datum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: choose point C on axis AB; for any small increment take AC increment CM and BC decrement CN in given ratio; with centres A,B and intervals AM, BN draw circles meeting in D; the D tangent point traces the desired curve. Corollary: taking A or B to infinity yields the Cartesian figures for refraction. Method is geometric: tangent-determination via intersecting circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a second attracting surface given a first to focus from A to B (Prop. XCVIII, Prob. XLVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, & circa axem AB descripta superficie quacunq; attractiva CD, regulari vel irregulari, per quam corpora de loco dato A exeuntia transire debent: invenire superficiem secundam attractivam EF, quæ corpora illa ad locum datum B convergere faciat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: intersect first and second surfaces with AB at C and E, choose D on intersection AB, set given sine ratios M:N, construct points G,H,K and draw KB, then with centre D describe circle through KB producet L and draw DL parallel BF; point F is tangent to the constructed EF which, revolved about AB, yields the required surface. The proposition includes algebraic ratio manipulations to ensure the trajectories lead to B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical design recommendations (Scholium after XCVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eadem methodo pergere liceret ad superficies tres vel plures. Ad usus autem Opticos maxime accommodatæ sunt figuræ Sphæricæ. ... Talia autem vitra Objectiva vitris Ellipticis & Hyperbolicis præferenda sunt, non solum quod facilius & accuratius formari possint, sed etiam quod penicillos radiorum extra axem vitri sitos accuratius refringant. Verum tamen diversa diversorum radiorum refrangibilitas impedimento est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: spherical, elliptic, hyperbolic surfaces have pros/cons; elliptic and hyperbolic lenses preferred for better off-axis ray correction; but chromatic dispersion (different refrangibility) limits perfection unless chromatic errors are otherwise corrected (e.g., by combining elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lost motion proportional to space for resistance ∝ velocity (Prop. I, Theor. I, Liber II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis, cui resistitur in ratione velocitatis, motus ex resistentia amissus est ut spatium movendo confectum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: if at each instant the motion lost is proportional to instantaneous velocity (i.e., resistance ∝ v), then integrating over time gives total lost motion proportional to distance moved. Corollary: if no gravity, total initial motion vs residual after some space gives proportion of spaces describable in infinite time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric progression of velocities and proportional spaces for linear resistance (Prop. II, Theor. II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpori resistitur in ratione velocitatis, & sola vi insita per Medium similare moveatur, sumantur autem tempora æqualia: velocitates in principiis singulorum temporum sunt in progressione Geometrica, & spatia singulis temporibus descripta sunt ut velocitates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via dividing time into equal parts and showing successive velocity ratios form a geometric progression; as a result distances per equal time are proportional to the velocities at the start of those intervals. Corollary gives graphical representation via hyperbola: time ↔ area, space ↔ abscissa, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion under gravity plus linear resistance; construction and consequences (Prop. III, Prob. I and corollaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis, cui dum in Medio similari recta ascendit vel descendit, resistitur in ratione velocitatis, quodq; ab uniformi gravitate urgetur, definire motum. ... Demonstration yields relations between areas, velocities at discrete times, maxima achievable velocity BC, and formulae linking space and time through constructed hyperbolic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a constructive method: represent gravity and resistance by rectilinear/hyperbolic constructs; deduces properties: maximum velocity attainable in descent, relationships of velocities at successive times (geometric progression), and relations between areas (times) and spaces. Several corollaries quantify max velocity vs instantaneous velocity, progression laws for times and velocities, and how space differences behave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectile motion with linear resistance; hyperbolic construction and empirical determination of resistance (Prop. IV, Prob. II and corollaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posito quod vis gravitatis in Medio aliquo similari uniformis sit, ac tendat perpendiculariter ad planum Horizontis; definire motum Projectilis, in eodem resistentiam velocitati proportionalem patientis. ... Describatur Hyperbola ... Projectile tempore DRtg perveniet ad punctum r, describens curvam lineam DraF ... Estq; velocitas ejus in puncto quovis r ut Curvæ Tangens rL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit geometric construction of trajectory via a hyperbola whose areas represent time; corollaries: relation to parabola in absence of resistance, methods to determine resistance and initial velocity from observed impact points (compare two projectiles launched with same speed at different angles and use computed vs observed ranges to infer resistance ratio), and how latus rectum scales with resistance and gravity. Scholium cautions linear-resistance is mathematical idealization; realistic fluids often give quadratic resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis: linear vs quadratic resistance and their regimes (Scholium at end of Prop. IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cæterum corpora resisti in ratione velocitatis Hypothesis est magis Mathematica quam Naturalis. ... In Mediis autem quæ rigore omni vacant (uti posthac demonstrabitur) corpora resistuntur in duplicata ratione velocitatum. Actione corporis velocioris communicatur eidem Medii quantitati, tempore minore, motus maior in ratione majoris velocitatis, adeoq; tempore æquali ... perturbatam) communicatur motus in duplicata ratione major, estq; resistentia ... ut motus communicatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit warning: linear resistance approximates slow motion in viscous-like media; in freely moving (non-rigid) media resistance ∝ v^2. The scholium motivates the next section which treats quadratic resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic-resistance motion properties (Prop. V, Theor. III, Sect. II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpori resistitur in velocitatis ratione duplicata, & sola vi insita per Medium similare movetur, tempora vero sumantur in progressione Geometrica a minoribus terminis ad majores pergente: dico quod velocitates initio singulorum temporum sunt in eadem progressione Geometrica inverse, & quod spatia sunt æqualia quæ singulis temporibus describuntur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resistance ∝ v^2, show by constructing hyperbolic relations that squares of velocities are proportional to their decrements, leading to velocities at starts of equal-time intervals forming an inverse geometric progression and distances in equal times being equal. Corollaries give graphical correspondences: represent time by an asymptotic segment and total space by hyperbolic area; provide ways to compute resistance relative to a centripetal force.
